rows.boundary_condition: Do not infer a standing requirement to search nonstop first, to choose a layover for price, or to add a stop to break up a long route unless the current request says so.
rows.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries that include or may include connections.

rows.exception_condition: Override this default if the user explicitly asks for nonstop only, requests a longer stopover, or prioritizes schedule, availability, or price over layover count and duration.
rows.name: flight_single_short_layover_preference
rows.preference_value: When a connecting flight is acceptable or needed, prefers no more than one layover and for the layover to be short.
rows.rationale: Across the three independent flight dialogues, the user consistently accepts or prefers only a limited layover pattern: one layover at most, and preferably short. The reason differs by trip—family cost tradeoff, visiting-family comfort, vacation flexibility—but the reusable policy is the same: avoid multiple or lengthy layovers.

semantic_review.reason: The examples consistently support limiting layovers to one and preferring a short connection when a layover is used. However, a general nonstop-first policy, cheaper-layover tradeoff, and long-haul route-break exception are not supported across all three instruction IDs, so those were removed.
